literal: Flute is sweet, lute is sweet, they say - their own children's prattling words those who have not heard.
translation: Only those who have not heard the prattling words of their own children will say that the flute and the lute are sweet.
modern: தங்கள் குழந்தைகளின் மழலைச் சொற்களைக் கேட்காதவர்கள் மட்டுமே குழலின் இசையும் யாழின் இசையும் இனிமையானவை என்று கூறுவார்கள்.
explanation: The couplet contrasts the beauty of instrumental music with the sound of a child's voice. It states that people praise the sweetness of the flute and the lute only until they hear their own children babble. The words 'குழல்' (flute) and 'யாழ்' (lute) represent the highest forms of refined music. Yet, the natural, unpolished 'மழலை' (prattle) of one's own children surpasses them in sweetness, highlighting the unparalleled joy of parenthood.
